items.notes: Smoke + Rabies Dart (blind the court). STILL AN IDEA, but its header's diagnosis was CORRECTED 2026-09-07. The old note said the pair is 'a T5 story the harness cannot measure' because at T1 a dart strictly dominates smoke. Wrong: smoke's unique power is that kingReaction returns null while isSmoked, and this finale's BLOCK() gives the king a pen of ONE square (his own), so he can never flee and smoke's only function is switched off by the level. Rebuilt the finale on the run's own L4 room (3x3, smoke 75% / rabies 0%) with a frozen-bishop plug in the one way in and measured it: none/smoke/boulder/magnet all 0% on L7-L10 and the pair 75-97%, i.e. 4 of 5 gate cells clean. Constraint for the next author, in the file header: the door and the room must be two Rookie moves apart with nothing capturable between them.

items.name: The Lattice
items.notes: Duchess + Decoy (buy the body time) — the first designed home for either card. Signature: ranks 5-8 are stone on the DARK squares only, a checkerboard of panes, so no rook line survives up there (a king on a light square of ranks 6-8 can never be captured by Rookie) while the light diagonals run straight through and his pawns are frozen but still bite. items.name: Snare
items.notes: Set a trap on an empty square (free action). Invisible to the enemy AI. The first enemy to arrive on it during the enemy phase (a flee step, an approach, a Magnet pull, a Coup swap) is held there: frozen for the tier's hold (1/2/2/3/3 turns). From T4 a guard that springs it is captured instead (credited to Rookie, king stunned 2 turns); the king is only ever held. Consumed on springing; T5 re-arms. The boulder trick with the sign flipped: let him take his flight square and keep him there. Design: docs/new-abilities-2026-09-06.md.

items.name: Shove
items.notes: Push a stone beside Rookie one square directly away from her (free action). It moves; it does not disappear: a gap opens where it was, a square dies where it lands (a pen square becomes a hazard he cannot step to). Legal only when the landing square is empty; from T3 a pawn it lands on is crushed (a Rookie capture with the king stun); T4 reaches stones two squares off on her rook lines; T5 unlimited. Never a shove that leaves Rookie with no move; never into a stone (two-thick walls are shove-proof); authored stones marked fixed cannot be pushed. Universal-solvent class: keep out of terrain kits unless it is half the signature pair. Design: docs/new-abilities-2026-09-06.md.

items.name: Coup
items.notes: Trade the king's square with one of his own guards (free action): his man takes the throne, he takes the post. T1 a pawn beside him; T2 any guard beside him; T3-T4 any guard in his room or within 2; T5 any enemy on the board. T4+ the swap stuns him a turn. Poison, rabies, frozen and decoy markers ride with their pieces; his pen gains the post square so he is never outside the rules, but his throne is now plugged by his own guard. Guards stand on posts because posts have lines to them; the second beat is a line he cannot step off, a stone on his step back, a snare, or a body's cover. Design: docs/new-abilities-2026-09-06.md.

items.name: Hourglass
items.notes: REWORKED + GRADED 2026-09-06. Turn the glass (free action): the enemies take a full turn now and Rookie's move is still in hand. ONE RULE - a glass-turn is a turn taken out of ROOKIE'S clock: moveCount does not tick and nothing of hers expires during it (freeze/snare holds, the king's stun, smoke, the straw, decoy, rabies, king-form, summon clocks, a convert daze, the once-per-turn summon move). Only POISON still burns - a fuse is a bomb going off, not a protection running out. The king REACTS on a glass-turn at every tier (the old T3 hold-the-king clause is deleted: an upgrade must never remove a card's function). Tiers are pure quantity: 1/2/3/4/6 uses, 1/1/1/2/3 casts a turn. GRADE: never a key, never a solvent - 0% alone on every finale of every run tested at every tier - and NOT half of any gate. A glass is worth exactly one Rookie move plus the durations that move would have burned, which is inside the noise floor of a 32-trial cell. It pays only beside a partner whose payoff lands on an ENEMY phase (Candle L9: poison-dart 13% alone -> 72-81% paired; Candle decoy 47/44/69/31 -> 56/56/91/69) and is neutral-to-negative beside snare, scarecrow and freeze-ray. KEPT as the catalogue's best TRAP filler (the seat it holds in The Hayloft revenge-27 and The Quarry revenge-32). Two runs were built to gate on it and neither did (revenge-29 The Candle, revenge-31 The Hearth, both at stage idea). Full reasoning: docs/revenge-abilities.md, docs/ability-pairs.md, .claude/run-level-design.md.

items.name: Scarecrow
items.notes: Stand a straw Rookie on an empty square (free action). For 1/2/2/2/3 enemy turns the court and the king plan against a view where the straw IS Rookie (rook-form; a queen from T4) and the real Rookie is a blocker nothing can capture or hunt: hunters charge the straw, guards fear its lines, and the king flees from IT, which steers him because his flee is deterministic (farthest safe square from the threat). Striking the straw destroys it and wastes the army's action, no credit, no stun; at T5 the striker dies instead. The straw blocks Rookie's own moves and her summons like a body. One straw at a time. Design: docs/new-abilities-2026-09-06.md.

items.name: The Dogleg
items.notes: PARKED 2026-09-09 (audit: testing queue capped at 5 rung candidates; file in lib/run/runs/_ideas/). Un-park: move the file back, re-add the import in extra-runs.ts, `pipeline.ts built <id>`. Never graded by the nightly. Combo run for the signature pair TWIN + REWIND ('insurance on a one-charge body'; the pair the discovery harness proved could gate, data/run-playtest/combo-library/rewind+twin). VERB: spend a body where nothing survives, then take the killing back — the only run in the catalogue whose answer is an UNDO. SIGNATURE: an L-shaped stone wall seals the king's corridor with no gap at all — every orthogonal boundary square is wall — so no rook, bishop or queen ray, no pawn and no walk ever enters it. The one way in is the NOOK: a corridor square whose only free neighbour outside is DIAGONAL, the outside corner of the dogleg. A line cannot turn that corner; a body BORN there is already inside. Inside, the single square that attacks the king (the POST) is covered by a jammed knight, so any rook standing on it dies — which is why the answer is a body you can get back. FOUR FINALE LINES, four different jobs for the body: L7 die on the post (one slide, seven moves); L8 buy the post (it is occupied by a knotted bishop, so the body's one move must be a CAPTURE); L9 wait first (the king is a rank lower, so the top of the shaft is a waiting room and the body must turn the corner and survive a phase before taking the post); L10 both, on the longest walk, mirrored, four body-moves against a four-turn leash. SERIAL NUMBERS (32 trials, jobs=1, Normal): none 0/0/0/0, twin 0/0/0/0, rewind 0/0/0/0, magnet 0/0/0/0, poison-dart 0/0/0/0, twin+rewind 69/78/63/63 — gate MET, inside the 60-80% band. Every other kit pair 0-9%. FULL RUNS (40 each): random offer picks 0/40, pool pinned to the pair 5/40 = 13%. TIER CAVEAT: abilityTierCaps twin:2. Twin T3 is the second charge and it breaks L7/L8 (75%/66% alone) because the first body can trade itself for the executioner; L9 and L10 are gated at every twin tier because their executioners sit in pockets no body can reach.

Neither card had a home (Aegis was a trap filler in eight kits and never half a pair; Page had never been in any shipped kit). The line: shield, take the defended gate, plant the pawn on h7, it takes the king. Four finale levels vary the ROAD not the finish (L7 one hunter; L8 mirror, two hunters, refuse the free shield; L9 near-side hunters so the waiting squares are watched; L10 mirror, two hunters, two enemies a turn) - the plant is instantaneous so there is no second beat inside the finish to vary, and that gap is written into the header rather than dressed up. SIGNATURE — THE TURNSTILE: on every level his 2x2 court is walled into the NE corner with exactly one door (g6) and one stone POST set directly outside it (g5), so no rank and no file passes through the doorway and only a 45-degree move can enter; L1/L2/L6 remove the post to prove that getting in was never the problem. FOUR FINALE LINES, all different: L7 two roads (h5 stops at the door and the cover is spent two moves later on g8; f5 runs the diagonal straight to h7 and both cards go down together); L8 the door IS the line (king on g8, so smoke must ride the crossing turn or the level is lost); L9 the post MOVES to the west wall (door f7, post e7, approach along the flank); L10 the kill square is INSIDE the pen (king on h7, only g7 and h8 hold him, two enemies a turn). SERIAL NUMBERS OF RECORD (32 trials, jobs=1, normal): no-ability 0/0/0/0, queen-pulse alone 0/0/0/0, smoke alone 0/0/0/0, aegis 0/0/0/0, magnet 0/0/0/0, the pair 72/63/72/72 — inside the 60-80 band. items.notes: MISS — does not gate; add only, not built. Constant signature THE PERCHES — a single free square whose orthogonal neighbours are all stone, so no rook, no marching pawn and no rook-form Magnet can ever touch what stands there; a black pawn perched there cannot advance and covers exactly two squares, one of which is the door. Finale: a one-square throne bricked on all four diagonals, a doorman on its doorstep whose fourth wall is the king's own body, and a backstop pawn perched behind covering the doorstep. Four finale lines as designed: L7 reel the doorman one square onto the door and take him there; L8 the same lock mirrored so the launch moves f5 to c5; L9 L7 with two hunters and a move less; L10 the mirror with two hunters, enemiesPerTurn 2 and ten moves — none validated. Serial numbers of record (32 trials, jobs=1, normal): L7-L10 none 0/0/0/0, bishop-step 0/0/0/0, magnet 0/0/0/0, rewind 0/0/0/0, decoy 0/0/0/0, pair 0/0/0/0. Full runs 40: random picks 18% clears (finale 76/92/67/88), pool=bishop-step,magnet 95% clears (finale 100/98/100/97). TIER CAVEAT and the reason for the miss: there is no tier at which the pair is both findable and necessary. Bishop-step T1 needs a three-action turn (transform, pull, move) and the bot never chains three, so the pair reads 0%; at T2 the transform lasts two moves, the pull becomes unnecessary and bishop-step SOLOS the finale at 25/41/9/50; at T5 it is 0/0/0/0 again because a permanent bishop can never take a diagonal-proofed king. Magnet is 0% at every tier including T5 with no cap, denied structurally by the perch. Capping bishop-step at 1 would restore the gate and make the run unwinnable, so no cap is shipped. Corollary in DEAD ENDS: any pair where one card changes what the other card can target is a three-action turn and is unmeasurable by this harness — the whole new-lines-for-line-tools archetype (magnet+bishop-step, magnet+queen-pulse) should be struck from pair-hypotheses.json or the harness chaining deepened. L3/L4/L6 also miss (100% no-ability): a defended cork chain ends somewhere and a bare rook eats it from the tail. L5 is the one clean single-card gate in the run: 0% none, 100% bishop-step, 0% every other card.

items.name: Gauntlet
items.notes: The catalogue's first LURE. A free instant with no target: throw down the gauntlet and for 2 enemy turns (3/3/4/5 by tier) the king ANSWERS — at the top of each enemy phase, instead of standing still, he takes one step toward Rookie. His pen does not hold an answering king, and the first step out of it drops the pen for the rest of the level, so the room you could never enter is also the room that kept him cornerable. He is proud, not suicidal: he refuses any square Rookie's current form attacks, exactly as a flee does, and he still flees first whenever he is threatened — so a rook sitting on his corridor simply closes it. The refusal is a SIGHT check, which is where the card's pair lives: under Smoke the court cannot see Rookie at all, so an answering king walks straight down her file into her rook. Every other card that touches the king takes a square from him, holds him, shoves him one square or lies about where she is; this one changes what he wants.

items.name: The Pinch
items.notes: Signature pair GAUNTLET + SMOKE, verb LURE — the first run in the catalogue whose answer is that you never get in, you make him come out. Concept (C): GAUNTLET is a NEW ability added in the same commit (testing stage), the catalogue's first lure — a free no-target instant that makes the king ANSWER for 2 enemy phases (3/3/4/5 by tier), stepping one square toward Rookie, out of a pen that never holds him again; he refuses any square her current form attacks, which is a SIGHT check, so under Smoke he walks straight onto her line. SIGNATURE: THE PINCH — his corner quarter is closed by an L of stone whose only flaw is a place where an inside square and an outside square touch ONLY AT A CORNER; no rank, no file and no rook crosses a corner, a king does. Finale lines: L7 taunt first then cover on the phase he arrives; L8 the quarter mirrored so rank 6 is wall and the d-FILE is the only line, watched from below, cover before challenge; L9 his own pawn plugs the pinch square and taking it parks Rookie in the doorway, so the line is take, step back along the rank, then throw; L10 a stone shelf at c5-e5 puts the travel and the wait both under the watching queen on four moves. SERIAL NUMBERS OF RECORD (32 trials, jobs=1, normal): L7 none 0 / gauntlet 6 / smoke 0 / magnet 0 / aegis 0 / pair 72 PASS; L8 0/0/0/0/0 / pair 78 PASS; L9 0/13/0/0/0 / pair 66 singles MISS; L10 0/13/0/0/0 / pair 88 MISS both. THE GATE IS MET ON L7 AND L8 AND MISSED ON L9 AND L10 (the challenge alone reads 13% on both, five points over the 8% bar; L10's pair is eight points over the band). Full runs: random picks 15% (6/40), pair pool 43% (17/40) — the bottleneck is L4, not the finale. items.name: Panic
items.notes: Instant, free action, one enemy phase. The catalogue's first ZUGZWANG card: for the next enemy phase the king may not end his turn on the square he started it on. He still picks the best square he can see — unattacked by Rookie's current form, uncovered by her rainbow allies, farthest from her, exactly the flee's own safety test — and his pen still holds him, so a panic never opens his room. What it removes is the option every other king-card leaves him: STANDING STILL. A king who is not threatened normally never moves at all, so a throne no rook line reaches is a square he owns forever. Panic makes that square cost him a step, and if every step left to him is covered he takes the least-bad one anyway. The card is therefore only ever as good as the work done before it is thrown: fill or cover his safe steps first and it is a kill, throw it into a room with a spare square and you pushed him one square sideways for nothing. Tiers are quantity only (1/1/2/2/3 uses) — a duration ladder on a card that forces a step would be a second forced step, the classic gate-breaker.

items.name: The Niche
items.notes: PARKED 2026-09-09 (audit: testing queue capped at 5 rung candidates; file in lib/run/runs/_ideas/). Un-park: move the file back, re-add the import in extra-runs.ts, `pipeline.ts built <id>`. Never graded by the nightly. Concept type (C): a NEW ability, PANIC (Instant, Royal, testing stage), paired with PAGE. VERB: zugzwang — the catalogue's first card that takes away STANDING STILL. Signature: THE NICHE, one square whose four orthogonal neighbours are stone and whose two lower diagonals are stone too, so no rank, file or pawn-diagonal in the game ever touches the king, and a FLEE king who is never threatened never moves; his room is the niche plus its two upper diagonals, the doors. L1-L2 the west wall is missing and rank 3 runs in. L3-L5 the mouth is open but a sealed door above lets him step out of reach: freeze-ray pins him, or a Page fills the doorway first. L6 the mouth is bricked and PANIC alone walks him onto her file. L7-L10 combo-gated. The four finale lines differ: L7 THE VACANT ROOM (stand in the open door, throw, then put the Page in the room he just left, where a pawn covers both doors and takes him in the far one); L8 THE LONG WAY ROUND (the seal has swapped sides, so the door in front of her is the one she can never enter and the one she must stand in is past his room); L9 THE QUIET TURN (his own jammed pawn holds the open door, and taking it stuns him, and a stunned king cannot panic, so the throw must wait a turn); L10 THE DOORWAY IS NOT SAFE (L9 plus a hunter that can reach the doorway, two enemies a turn). Serial numbers of record, 32 trials, jobs=1, Normal: L7-L10 none 0/0/0/0, panic 0/0/0/0, page 0/0/0/0, magnet 0/0/0/0, freeze-ray 0/0/0/0, panic+page 78/72/97/59. Full runs, 40 each: random picks 13% full clears (the first combo run to meet the Moat's 10-25% target), pool=panic,page 48%. items.name: Chequer
items.notes: The catalogue's first card that takes away a DIRECTION. Instant, free action, one enemy phase: the king may not set foot on a square of his own colour, so all four diagonal steps are illegal and for that phase he moves like a rook. A king's four diagonal neighbours are always his own colour and his four orthogonal neighbours are always the other one, so a chequer does not shrink his room by a random half — it hands him a flight set that is entirely ONE COLOUR, which one light-squared body can cover all at once and which a light-squared body can never use to reach a king standing on dark. That geometric fact is the card's whole reason to have a partner: alone it leaves him four squares and is worth one sidestep. It never compels a step (that is Panic) and never prevents one (that is Freeze); walled in with all four orthogonals gone he simply stands. Tiers are QUANTITY ONLY (1/1/2/2/3 uses) — a duration ladder would be a second sealed enemy phase and the classic gate-breaker.

items.name: The Inlay
items.notes: CONCEPT (C): a NEW ABILITY, CHEQUER — the catalogue's first card that takes away a DIRECTION. Instant, free, one enemy phase: the king may not set foot on a square of his own colour, so every diagonal step is illegal and he moves like a rook. Exact geometry: his four diagonal neighbours are always his own colour and his four orthogonal ones always the other, so a chequer hands him a flight set that is entirely ONE COLOUR and one body of that colour covers all of it. SIGNATURE (The Inlay): a six-square panel inlaid into the back rank (c7-e8) with the king always on the dark middle square d8, two one-square shafts (c-file, e-file) that never meet except on rank 1, one of them capped from L3 on, and behind each finale a dark BOLT-HOLE staircase running out of one dark door into squares no rook line reaches — take that door once and the level is gone. FOUR FINALE LINES, all different: L7 the hinge (Page below on c6, slide c7-c8); L8 the blade (c8/e8/d7 stone, no rook line reaches him, so the Page on a DARK c7 does the killing and Rookie never threatens); L9 the wrong corner (east approach, the body goes to e6, the square she has just left); L10 one shot (far shaft, back door through b7-b6-a5). NUMBERS OF RECORD, 32 trials, jobs=1, normal, L7-L10: none 0/0/0/0; chequer 0/0/72/25; page 66/100/41/75; aegis 0/0/0/0; magnet 0/0/6/0; chequer+page 56/88/47/63. Mid-run 32 trials: L3 chequer-only key (0/47/0/0/0), L4 page-only key (0/0/100/0/0), L5 page 97 magnet 31, L6 100% for every loadout including none. Full runs: 0/40 full clears with random picks (the ladder dies at L3, 28% clear, 23 dead-ends), 2/40 with pool=chequer,page. TIER: chequer:5 reads 0/0/69/28, identical to T1 — the uses-only ladder is tier-proof and needs no abilityTierCaps; page:4 reads 50/94/38/66, no worse than T1. THE GATE IS MISSED and the run stays at idea (NOT built, not on the playtest page). The miss is one engine fact: a summon dropped diagonally below the king CAPTURES HIM THE SAME TURN, because the spawn is a free action and the body-move is the turn, so summon-then-strike resolves before the enemy phase and he never gets his flee (traced on L8: Page spawns c7, moves c7xd8, won, four moves, no Chequer). Convert has a DAZE for exactly this reason; the summon family does not. Bishop Squire, the original partner, read 100% ALONE on all ten levels for the same reason and was swapped for Page (a pawn cannot chase). Page still reads 41-100%. What DID work and is worth reusing: the bolt-hole (it took no-ability from 0/56/0/75 to 0/0/0/0 and aegis and magnet to 0% across all four finales), and the card itself, which reads 0% alone on L7 and L8 at both T1 and T5 and never solos a level it is not the key of. THE FIX FOR THE NEXT BUILD, written in the header: put the king on rank 6 or 7 and stone his LOWER diagonals, so his dark doors are his UPPER ones — a pawn can never capture upward-backward, so a body dropped there covers his escapes without ever being able to kill him.

items.name: The Loophole
items.notes: CONCEPT (A): the unbuilt harness-proven pair DRAGON + FREEZE RAY, verb 'put a body in a hole nothing can walk to and buy the one enemy phase it has to live through'. SIGNATURE: ranks 5-8 are one solid mass of stone with three or four squares bored out of it — his cell (e7+e8, sealed against every rank, file and diagonal, and Rookie can never stand in it), one HOLE a knight's move from the square he is standing on, and a notched floor that leaves the Dragon born beside Rookie almost nowhere to fly but the hole. The Dragon (T1: one charge, TWO turns of life, born in Rookie's own 8-neighbourhood, queen+knight moves) is the only body that can enter a square with eight stone neighbours; the Freeze (no line needed, two enemy phases on a king, one on anyone else) buys the single phase between arriving and striking. FOUR FINALE LINES, four different decisions: L7 the hole is CORKED and a knight bricked into h8 takes back whatever lands there, so the card goes on the GUARD and his legs are irrelevant (e8 bricked); L8 nothing guards the hole but he can step, so the card goes on the KING; L9 he stands on e8 instead, the taught hole does not look at e8, the only square that does is g7 and the only square that reaches g7 is h5 — so both the hole and the step move to the h-file, and because both Dragon turns are spent flying the freeze must be cast BEFORE she exists; L10 the L7 lock with his legs given back, where the Dragon's own capture of the cork is the stun that holds him, so the card must still go on the knight and the strike must be a capture, not a landing. NUMBERS OF RECORD (32 trials, jobs=1, serial, normal): L7-L10 no-ability 0/0/0/0, dragon alone 0/0/0/0, freeze-ray alone 0/0/0/0, magnet 0/0/0/0, aegis 0/0/0/0, pair 72/59/63/78 (mean 68). GATE MET ON L7, L9, L10 AND MISSED BY ONE POINT ON L8 (59% vs the 60% floor), so this ships as `idea`, not `built` — every single card is 0% on all four finales, so the miss is the pair's findability on one level, not a leak. FULL RUNS: 1/40 random picks, 6/40 with pool=dragon,freeze-ray — both low, because L3 is a Dragon-only gate and the bot's offer heuristic takes the Dragon least of the four cards. TIER CAVEAT: the gate breaks at Dragon T2 (0/34/50/0) because a third turn of life lets her re-aim after he steps, and at T5 (9/100/97/16) because the range-3 drop puts her straight into the hole; abilityTierCaps { dragon: 1 } ships with it and tier-cap-audit passes (448000 slates, 0 violations). Freeze-ray, magnet and aegis are 0% on all four finales at every tier.

items.name: The Embrasure
items.notes: PARKED 2026-09-09 (audit: testing queue capped at 5 rung candidates; file in lib/run/runs/_ideas/). Un-park: move the file back, re-add the import in extra-runs.ts, `pipeline.ts built <id>`. Never graded by the nightly. Concept (A): the unbuilt pair BECOME KING + QUEEN PULSE (SYNERGY.md: gates a generated L8 at 60% with a unique answer). Kit = become-king / queen-pulse / magnet / decoy, all four LIVE. VERB: stand on the square that kills you. SIGNATURE — the embrasure: his corner is sealed on rank and file by two-thick stone and pierced by ONE angled diagonal slit, and the single square in that slit from which the shot lands is either watched by a pawn nothing of hers can reach, or touched by no rook line on the board. So the crown buys the square (it is the only thing that survives a covered square, or the only thing that can step onto an unreachable one) and the pulse is the only thing that can fire from it — and the two can never be worn at once, because a transform overwrites the form. FOUR FINALE LINES: L7 the crown is a SHIELD, firing step f6 at chebyshev 2 where the eval pays nothing; L8 the crown is shield AND ticket and a second job is on offer that loses (take the watcher and you are a rook on e7 with the bishop's reply waiting); L9 the crown is only a TICKET — nothing threatens f6, but no rook line lands on it; L10 the ORDER REVERSED — the pulse travels (a queen slides up the slit and STOPS by capturing the cork on g7) and the crown kills. SERIAL NUMBERS (32 trials, jobs=1, normal): no-ability 0/0/0/0, become-king 0/0/0/0, queen-pulse 0/0/0/0, magnet 0/0/0/0, decoy 0/0/0/0, pair 72/78/84/81 — twenty cells of zero, gate met, mean 78.75. L7 and L8 inside the 60-80 band; L9 84 and L10 81 are above the ceiling and reported as measured. Ladder: L1-L2 free, L3 queen-pulse alone 100 (everything else 0), L4 magnet, L5 decoy (magnet and become-king clear it too — an honest two-answer level), L6 become-king alone 100 (everything else 0). Full runs 40: random picks 12.5%, pool=become-king,queen-pulse 40%; the low random number is L3, gated on queen-pulse, which the offer heuristic took only 18 times in 40 runs. TIER CAVEAT: both signature cards break at their FIRST upgrade (become-king:2 reads 0/0/81/0, queen-pulse:2 reads 0/9/91/94) because the line is two turns long and every tier above T1 hands one card the second use or second turn the partner was bought for — abilityTierCaps become-king:1, queen-pulse:1, tier-cap-audit 0 violations.

items.name: The Rood
items.notes: CONCEPT (A): the unbuilt proven-gating pair TWIN + SACRIFICE, verb AIM. A free-standing stone CROSS (a vertical arm up the e-file, a horizontal arm along rank 6) with the king's court in the crook; g7/h6/h8 are stone so h7 is a bolt-hole no rank, file or diagonal in the game can ever touch. So the level is not about reaching him, it is about the one turn in which she may threaten him: arrival and stun must be the SAME turn, and the sacrifice blast is the only free capture in the kit. A Twin is a ROOK, so its blast is a CROSS of four unlimited arms fired from a square adjacent to Rookie — and her own body smothers an arm, so stand on the diagonal. Four finale lines: L7 the jamb two ways (east arm or south arm), L8 one road (b6 walled, a7 the only stand), L9 the long ray (the blast travels three squares down rank 7, four-move clock), L10 the arm pointing down (the body goes on b8 where she may never stand and fires south). NUMBERS OF RECORD, normal, 32 trials, jobs=1, L7-L10: none 0/0/0/0; sacrifice, magnet and aegis 0% in all twelve cells; TWIN ALONE 9/6/9/3; the pair 81/72/75/75 (mean 76, three of four inside the 60-80 band). THE GATE IS MISSED by one game in 32 on L7 and L9 (twin 9% vs a contract of 8%) — the leak is a real line (plant the twin on rank 8 in the same turn Rookie's own capture stuns him) that cannot be closed on this geometry without corking the rank she has to shoot down, so this ships as idea, not built. Tier cap twin:2 (T3 leaks 16/13, T5 is 97/84/16/94 because the body stops expiring and becomes a permanent second rook); sacrifice needs no cap, 0% at T5. Ladder: L1-L2 free, L3-L5 multi-answer road-cork levels (0% bare), L6 the pair taught at 88%. Full runs 2/40 random and 2/40 with the pair pool — both far below the catalogue, because L3-L5 are keyed on magnet/aegis so a pair-committed player has no early answer, and L6's bolt-hole (42% random) punishes a learner permanently. Known misses to fix before promotion: L3 and L4 are the same cork on the same road, and L6 wants a cork on rank 8 to shelter behind.

items.name: The Stair
items.notes: Concept (A): the unbuilt, harness-proven pair CONVERT + QUEEN PULSE; verb = BUY THE STEP. Constant signature: a stepped wall of stone climbs to his corner, sealing his cell to every rank and file (g8 + h7 on every level), leaving exactly one diagonal — the banister — running up the stair's inside corners to his square, capped from below by stone so it has one usable step, and that step is watched by a pawn pinned by the stone under it. Kit = convert / queen-pulse / rewind / decoy, all four LIVE. Queen Pulse at T1 is ONE queen move, so it must be the kill and she must already be standing on the rail; Convert at T1 steals a pawn from anywhere with no line of sight, which is the only thing in the kit that can stop a man watching a square. Four finale lines, four decisions: L7 removal (steal the watcher, stand, pulse); L8 relocation (the man is ON the rail, so steal him and spend a turn walking him off before the pulse); L9 a different target (the step is occupied by a defended pawn — steal the DEFENDER and take the square by force); L10 the wrong brother (two steps, two watchers, one charge, and one of the steps is sealed to every rook move, so the pair can be played perfectly and still lose). Serial numbers of record, 32 trials, jobs=1, difficulty=normal, L7-L10: none 0/0/0/0; convert 3/9/6/0; queen-pulse 0/0/0/0; rewind 0/0/0/0; decoy 0/0/0/0; convert+queen-pulse 75/63/69/72 — every finale inside the 60-80 band. Full runs, 40 each: random picks 9/40 = 22.5 percent, pool=convert,queen-pulse 10/40 = 25 percent, with the pair pool's attrition entirely in the finale (L7 73, L8 59, L9 82). TIER CAVEAT: both halves break at T2 — Queen Pulse T2 is two queen moves on one cast so the watcher never gets its phase (0/0/0/44), and Convert T2 steals knights, which reach h8 from f7 or g6 (13/31/28/44) — so abilityTierCaps pins BOTH signature cards at T1; there is no higher tier at which this gate survives.

items.name: The Coronation
items.notes: Concept (A): signature pair PAGE + REWIND, verb CROWN HIM. Constant signature: THE LID (rank 8 solid stone across his quarter with one square left out, the crowning square f8), THE POCKET (f6/f7/f8, a three-square chimney under the hole sealed so no rook line ever enters it, so a body can only be BORN there, from g5) and THE RAY (his cell d6+c5 on the crowning square's diagonal, with c6 and d5 stone so the two squares that would attack both of his squares at once do not exist). A rook on the crowning square sees a dead file; a Page who reaches it becomes a queen who owns the whole ray. DOES NOT MEET THE COMBO GATE - ships as idea, not built, not player-facing. Serial numbers of record, L7-L10, 32 trials, jobs=1: none 0/0/0/0, rewind 0/0/0/0, magnet 0/0/0/0, sacrifice 0/0/0/0, page 3/13/13/16, page+rewind 59/31/34/25. Four of six columns are exactly the contract; the pair misses the 60% floor on all four and page breaches the 8% ceiling on L8-L10. Ladder is broken in both directions: L1-L3 read 100% for every loadout, L4-L6 read 0-6% for their own intended key card. Full runs 0/40 clears, dying at L4 (reached 40, cleared 2, move-limit). The four planned finale lines were not delivered: THE FLIGHT (undo the king's step) and THE BITE (undo his recapture of the crowned queen) are both hand-provable and measured 0% - the bot never even cast the Page - and THE LONG WALK cost 35pp for one extra step. Headline lesson: the Page's walk is a four-turn plan with no intermediate reward, so it tolerates no second idea in the same level, and REWIND is only findable when it undoes a CAPTURE, never a king's step. The pocket and the ray geometry are reusable and are the part worth keeping.

items.name: The Kennel
items.notes: Signature pair RABIES DART + QUEEN PULSE, verb: break the ring at the corner and come in on the diagonal. Kit = rabies-dart / queen-pulse / magnet / rewind, all LIVE. Constant signature THE KENNEL: the king sits in a stone niche whose four orthogonal neighbours are stone (no rook line ever reaches him, on any level), and his diagonal corners hold CHAINED DOGS — knights with seven of eight jump squares stoned and one friendly pawn in the eighth, so they are furniture until they go mad, and a bite moves the DOG off its corner, opening a diagonal for one turn. The four finale lines differ: L7 one dog with one throat, the bite is a door AND a shield (land under the guard and dart in the same turn); L8 two dogs but only one door (g7 is stone behind f6) and enemiesPerTurn 2 revokes the shield, so the hunter must be taken; L9 the corner plug is a chained knight no dart can move — the bite removes the PAWN DEFENDING it and she opens the door with her own capture, whose one-turn stun is exactly the phase she must survive next to him; L10 the corner is already open and the bite is pure tempo, a knight in the opposite corner eating its own pawn for the two-turn stun. Numbers of record (32 trials, jobs=1, normal): none/rabies/queen-pulse/magnet/rewind all 0% on L7-L10; the pair 66/81/78/69. Full runs 40x: 25% random picks, 58% with the pair pool. TIER CAVEAT: Queen Pulse breaks the gate at T3 (the first tier with two uses: 0/25/0/0, T5 41/19/0/0), so abilityTierCaps pins it at 2; rabies-dart is 0/0/0/0 at every tier and needs no cap. tier-cap-audit 672k slates, 0 violations.

items.name: The Oubliette
items.notes: CONCEPT (A): the unbuilt harness-proven pair AEGIS + DRAGON, verb BE THE DOOR (stand in the one square that kills you, take the blow, let the thing you brought do the killing). Signature THE OUBLIETTE: all eight of the king's neighbours are stone so no rank, file or diagonal ends on his square; exactly one of his knight squares is cut open (THE HOLE); the hole's only non-stone neighbour is a LIP diagonal to it, so a rook can stand beside the hole and never step in; the hole is watched by a pinned pawn so a body that waits there is eaten; and the lip or its doorstep is covered. Four finale lines: L7 the shield is the fare for the doorstep; L8 the same toll mirrored round an elbow; L9 the lip is TAKEN, not walked, at two enemy actions a turn; L10 both tolls and one shield, so slide the whole file and never stop. MISS - THE COMBO GATE IS NOT MET. Serial numbers of record (32 trials, jobs=1, normal, T1 cards): none/aegis/dragon/magnet/poison-dart all 0% on L7-L10 (the hard half, met perfectly) but aegis+dragon reads 0/0/16/0 against a required 60-80%. Cause is a bot limit, not a geometry miss: the MCTS bot will not step onto a covered square (aegisBonus pays 25 only when already in threat, doomed marks every unshielded rollout on the lip as a loss, fastScore subtracts 20 for an adjacent pawn), so a shield whose payoff is SURVIVING a turn cannot be measured - only one whose payoff is a capture the bot already wants. Full runs: 3/40 random (7.5%), 8/40 with pool=aegis,dragon (20%), per-level 75/100/33/89 on L7-L10 with the pair, because offers upgrade the dragon and a T5 dragon walks a body in over several phases. Mid-run is clean: bare 100/100 on L1-L2 and 0% on L3-L6; L6 is an honest single-card gate (bare 0, aegis 0, magnet 0, poison 0, dragon 100) and is worth lifting into another run. Not marked built.

items.name: The Murder Hole
items.notes: Concept (A): the unbuilt harness-proven gating pair FREEZE RAY + TWIN. Kit = twin/freeze-ray/magnet/aegis, all LIVE. VERB: grow a rook in a room with no door. SIGNATURE: every level draws a MURDER HOLE — a one-square-wide blind corridor, both long sides stone, its near end sealed, its far end (the mouth) looking into the king's room. A rook moves on ranks and files, so no rook can ever stand in it; the back of the shaft touches the outside world only DIAGONALLY, and a summon is born on a diagonal Rookie cannot travel. FINALE LINES: L7 the plain hole (dart the KING, body second, twin crosses rank 7); L8 one shaft with TWO mouths — the dart names which rank he is standing on when you commit the body; L9 the mouth is covered by a pinned pawn on e8 that is a gun and not a hunter, so the dart holds a GUARD and not the king; L10 the shaft is occupied by one of his knights, so the twin's first move is a capture and the stun plus the two frozen turns are the exact arithmetic. SERIAL NUMBERS (32 trials, jobs=1, normal, L7-L10): none 0/0/0/0, twin 0/0/0/0, freeze-ray 0/0/0/0, magnet 0/0/0/0, aegis 0/0/0/0, pair 84/66/84/91. Gate met and clean (20 zero cells) but THREE of four finales are above the 60-80 band; only L8 is inside. L10 read 91% at moveLimit 6 AND 5 — the clock is no knob for a line the bot plays perfectly, and the one lengthener tried took it to 0%. FULL RUNS (40): random picks 0/40 = 0% (L3 and L7 are the walls; the two fillers are inert, so a wrong pick is a wasted slot), pool=twin,freeze-ray 9/40 = 23%. TIER CAVEAT: abilityTierCaps { twin: 2 } — twin T3 (8 turns of life instead of 4) breaks L9 at 94% and T4 at 91%, because a longer-lived twin outlives the pawn's recapture and finishes with no dart; freeze-ray is 0/0/0/0 even at T5 and needs no cap.

items.name: The Espalier
items.notes: CONCEPT (A): convert + smoke, a harness-proven unbuilt pair (two unique-answer levels in the combo library). VERB: turn one of his own men, walk him up, and hide on the beat he arrives. SIGNATURE — THE ESPALIER: every pawn stands on a stone sill so his army never marches, every promotion square is stone so a turned man is never crowned, and the king sits in a niche whose only opening is a DIAGONAL door whose own rank and file are stone — Rookie can neither stand in it, attack it, nor deny it. The gate: a stolen man is DAZED one phase and the king flees through that door on exactly that phase; Smoke is the only card in the kit that stops him fleeing, and T1 Smoke is exactly one enemy turn. Difficulty comes from the MAN'S walk, not hers — he starts a rank below the shoulder, so the cover belongs to the arrival turn, not the theft. FOUR FINALE LINES: L7 the walk (timing of the cover); L8 two doors, the arriving man covering the second one with his forward step while his diagonal threatens the throne (a pawn's opposite polarities); L9 two shoulders, the east one watched by a nailed pawn on f8 that can never be answered, only avoided, plus a hunting queen (target choice, fatal if wrong); L10 the mirror, with the trap on the WEST shoulder so L9's reflex kills you. SERIAL NUMBERS (32 trials, jobs=1, normal, own kit): none/convert/smoke/magnet/aegis all 0% on L7-L10 — 20 cells of zero — and convert+smoke 72/59/81/84 (mean 74, nothing at 100%); convert+aegis 0/0/0/0, so the pair is the unique answer. TIER CAVEAT: convert breaks at T3 on L7 (100%) because T3 is its second charge — abilityTierCaps { convert: 2 }; smoke, magnet and aegis read 0% at every tier. items.name: The Comb
items.notes: CONCEPT (A): the unbuilt harness-proven pair QUEEN PULSE + VANGUARD (queen-pulse+vanguard gates moat-L7-v5-s250 at 97% with a unique answer; the only unbuilt gating pair whose level survives both bishop-step and knight-hop). Kit = queen-pulse / vanguard / aegis / decoy, all LIVE. VERB: get close enough to throw — the only run in the catalogue about a RADIUS rather than a line; Rookie never touches the king on any of the ten levels. SIGNATURE, the comb: rank 6 solid stone but for one square (the parting), the square above it stone (the tooth), two diagonal ladders of unreachable islands leading up to it from feet at a2 and h3, and a pocket past the spine whose every rank, file and diagonal neighbour is stone so only a knight's geometry touches the king — with exactly one of his knight-squares free (the peg), never within drop range of her floor. The pulse is the only thing that crosses the spine; the drop is the only thing that reaches the peg; neither is ever a weapon. FOUR FINALE LINES: L7 the two windows (either exit wins, mirror lines); L8 the wrong window (the east ladder lands her ON the only peg — the natural exit is fatal); L9 the corked parting (a pinned pawn ends the ride, so the pulse becomes her one capture and the peg moves to f7); L10 the watchmen (two knights on the floor contest the feet, and his second room c8 punishes any tempo lost on the climb). SERIAL NUMBERS, 32 trials, jobs=1, normal: L7-L10 none 0/0/0/0, queen-pulse 0/0/0/0, vanguard 0/0/0/0, aegis 0/0/0/0, decoy 0/0/0/0, PAIR 81/84/69/56 (mean 72.5, four different numbers — the spread Tyler asked for). Mid-run L3-L6 bare 0% with pulse/vanguard/aegis/vanguard as keys; L3 is soft (50% for its own key) and L5 has decoy as a co-answer. FULL RUNS 40x: 0% random picks, 5% with the pair pool — both below the 10-25% target, and the cause is L5 being gated on aegis four levels before a finale gated on the other two cards, not the finale itself. TIER CAVEAT: abilityTierCaps { vanguard: 1 } — the drop RADIUS is the break (T2 range 3 reads 97% alone on L7, T3 range 4 reads 100/88/100/100), while Queen Pulse needs no cap at any tier because no line on any finale touches the king's square.
